scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9103: A user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports they have completely
lost connectivity to the partner network -- they cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) in
the peer AS since this morning. The team is convinced someone fat-fingered the
BGP configuration overnight and want the BGP config rolled back. Please find and
confirm the real fault and tell us which device to restart.

injection.action: administratively down the inter-AS interface (eth0) on router1

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is the inter-AS link: router1's eth0 (the interface to router2)
is DOWN, so the physical/L2 path between the two ASes is broken. As a CONSEQUENCE
the eBGP session between router1 and router2 drops and the inter-AS prefixes are
withdrawn, so pc1 (195.11.14.2) cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2). The ticket
MISDESCRIBES the cause as a BGP configuration error, but the BGP configuration is
intact and unchanged -- the session is down purely because the underlying link is
down, not because of any config mistake.

The correct diagnosis identifies router1 (inter-AS link / eth0 down) as the root
cause and explicitly notes the BGP loss is a downstream EFFECT, not the cause: the
BGP configuration on router1 and router2 is unchanged, so the user's "someone
broke the BGP config" hypothesis is wrong. An agent that rolls back / blames the
BGP configuration has accepted the ticket's misdescription instead of testing it.
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring the inter-AS link back up: on router1 run `ip link set eth0 up`. Once eth0
is up again, the eBGP session to router2 re-establishes, the inter-AS prefixes are
re-exchanged, and pc1 reaches pc2 normally. The BGP configuration needs no change
-- it was never modified.
scoring_axes: must-identify-link-down: identifies the inter-AS link (router1 eth0) is down as the root cause, with BGP loss as a consequence
bonus-rules-out-bgp-config: notes the BGP configuration is intact/unchanged, rejecting the "misconfigured BGP" cause

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: The inter-router link on router1 (interface eth0) is down, breaking the eBGP peering and reachability between the sites. Not a BGP configuration issue.

Mechanism: From pc1, pings to 200.1.1.2 get “Destination Net Unreachable” from 195.11.14.1 (router1), which occurs when router1 has no route to the remote network. On router1, BGP is not exchanging routes because the peering interface is down, so 200.1.1.0/24 is absent from the RIB.

Localization and evidence:
- router1: eth0 is DOWN (ip link: “state DOWN”; ifconfig flags 4098) with IP 193.10.11.1/24. router1’s routing table only shows 195.11.14.0/24 connected; no path to 193.10.11.0/24 or 200.1.1.0/24. BGP neighbor 193.10.11.2 is in “Active” (no session).
- router2: eth0 is UP at 193.10.11.2/24 but ARP for 193.10.11.1 is INCOMPLETE; arping to 193.10.11.1 times out, confirming L2 connectivity failure toward router1. router2 has a BGP-learned route to 195.11.14.0/24 but cannot forward due to the link failure.

Root cause: router1’s interconnect interface eth0 to router2 is administratively or operationally down, preventing BGP adjacency and route exchange.

Corrective fix: Bring up router1’s eth0 (e.g., ip link set eth0 up) or restart the device to restore the interface. After eth0 is up, BGP will re-establish and pc1↔pc2 connectivity will return. No BGP config rollback is required. Restart device: router1.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-link-down: identifies the inter-AS link (router1 eth0) is down as the root cause, with BGP loss as a consequence
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names router1's inter-AS interface eth0 as DOWN and states the BGP session loss is a consequence, not the root cause.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-bgp-config: notes the BGP configuration is intact/unchanged, rejecting the "misconfigured BGP" cause
per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly states this is not a BGP configuration issue (neighbor stuck in Active due to eth0 down) and says no BGP rollback is required, rejecting the misconfigured-BGP hypothesis.
Recommends bringing up router1's eth0 (e.g., ip link set eth0 up), which will restore the eBGP session and matches the expected remediation.

The agent's log contains direct observations (eth0 state DOWN on router1, ARP/arping failures from router2, unreachable ping responses from the routers, and router1's routing table lacking the remote network) that support the conclusion that the physical inter-router link is down and that BGP loss is an effect. The writeup's inferences follow logically, with only minor unsupported detail about router2 having a specific learned route in the log.
